title: Events, Not Pixels: Where World Models Get the Return Wrong
abstract: arXiv:2610.29435v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World models are increasingly used for planning, where a planner ranks candidate actions by returns imagined by the model. However, these models are judged mainly by how well they render frames, even though a visually faithful rollout can still assign the wrong return. To identify where this mismatch arises, we introduce a transition-level diagnostic that replaces imagined transitions with real ones and measures the reduction in return error against a budget-matched random control. Our analysis yields two findings. (1) Event transitions, the few steps where a reward is earned or an episode ends, are rendered as well as other steps (median pixel-error ratio 0.85), yet restoring them removes a median of 70% of the return error. In contrast, restoring transitions with the largest MSE, SSIM or LPIPS error removes less than a random choice. translated_title: 事件而非像素：世界模型在回报估计上的失误所在
translated_abstract: 世界模型正越来越多地被用于规划，其中规划器依据模型想象出的回报对候选动作进行排序。然而，这些模型主要依据其渲染帧的质量来评判，即使视觉上逼真的 rollout 也可能给出错误的回报。为了找出这种不匹配的根源，我们引入了一种转换级别的诊断方法：用真实转换替换想象转换，并以预算匹配的随机对照为基准测量回报误差的减少量。我们的分析得出两个发现：(1) 事件转换——即获得奖励或回合结束的少数关键步骤——的渲染质量与其他步骤相当（像素误差比中位数为 0.85），但恢复这些转换可消除中位数 70% 的回报误差。相比之下，恢复具有最大 MSE、SSIM 或 LPIPS 误差的转换，其效果还不如随机选择。在通过我们可靠性检验的 44 个 Atari-100k 模型-数据配对中，包括三个相关的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 世界模型在规划中的回报误差主要来自对“事件转换”（获得奖励或回合结束的关键步骤）的误判，而非整体像素渲染质量——仅恢复这些关键步骤的真实转换即可消除约 70% 的回报误差。
en_tdlr: Return errors in world-model planning stem mainly from mispredicted event transitions—the rare steps where rewards are earned or episodes end—rather than overall pixel fidelity, as restoring just these transitions removes a median 70% of the return error.
